architecture.mechanism: Breaking an infrared beam of light sensed by a photodiode, with the photodiodes connected to comparators, yields a discrete direction-resolved electrical signal that a controller uses to govern automated door actuation.
architecture.intervention: Add an infrared emitter/photodiode pair with comparator across the Odyssey sliding door latch and feed its beam-break output into the powertrain control module as a verified latch-state interlock: above a motion threshold the unlatch signal inhibits the engine-shutdown command and issues a driver alert instead of stalling, while permitting normal door actuation when stationary.
architecture.expected_effect: An unintended sliding-door unlatch at 65 mph is detected and converted into a hold/warning action, so the engine continues running during vehicle motion while sliding door operation is preserved when parked.
architecture.falsification_test: On a closed track, drive at 65 mph and command a sliding-door unlatch; pass if engine speed remains stable with no stall, fail if the engine stalls; separately confirm with the vehicle parked that the door still opens and closes normally.
